sections.html:
Scott County sits on the Mississippi River in eastern Iowa as part of the Quad Cities metro. Davenport is the county seat and the largest city, with 101,724 residents in 2020. Bettendorf follows at 39,102, then Eldridge (6,726), LeClaire (4,710), Park View (2,709), Durant (1,871), Blue Grass (1,666), Walcott (1,551), Buffalo (1,176) and Princeton (923).

Each community has its own school and city-service area, which is why one county tax bill can look quite different from one address to the next. Check where your house sits before you compare it to a neighbor's.

Scott County has two assessors. The Scott County Assessor covers everything except the City of Davenport, and Davenport has its own City Assessor. Both offices are on the fifth floor of the Scott County Administrative Center in Davenport.

A house in Bettendorf, Eldridge or a rural township goes through the county assessor. A house inside Davenport goes through the city assessor. The county's records search lets you look up assessor, auditor and treasurer records by name, address or parcel number, and Davenport City Assessor records appear in the same search. Read the parcel record before you call so you reach the right office the first time.

The Board of Review hears assessment protests from April 2 through April 30 under Iowa Code 441.37. Call the assessor that covers your parcel to learn how to file, and ask whether an informal review is offered before you go formal.

sections.h2: Due dates and how to pay
sections.html:
Property tax is billed in two equal installments, due September 30 and March 31 of the following year. A due date that lands on a weekend or holiday moves to the next business day. Taxes are certified in July or August.

Interest starts on the first business day after each due date, so a payment that arrives a day late is already delinquent. Call the Treasurer for the current rate before you work out a payoff.

Payment methodWhereFee
CashCounter onlyNone

E-checkOnline$0.25
Credit cardCounter or online2.25%

The Treasurer works from two locations in Davenport: the Scott County Administrative Center at 600 W. 4th St., and the Scott County General Store at 902 W. Kimberly Rd., Suite 6D. Mail payments to 600 W 4th St, Davenport, IA 52801-1003. Both locations have a drop box for checks, and visitors with an appointment are seen first.

Delinquent taxes are published in June and sold at the annual tax sale on the third Monday of June. The buyer receives a certificate. If nobody buys after two publications, the certificate goes to Scott County. When the taxes are not redeemed within the period set by law, the certificate holder can receive a deed, and county-held properties are usually auctioned.

If you are behind, the calendar matters more than any one number:

  • September 30 and March 31 are the due dates, and interest can begin the next business day.
  • June is when delinquent parcels are published.
  • The third Monday of June is the sale.
  • Redemption stays open until the legal period runs out.

Selling before the sale date is one way to remove the lien from your title. A cash buyer can often close fast enough to pay the county from the proceeds, but get the exact payoff from the Treasurer first.

The Scott County Recorder will not accept a deed that lacks the required statements and blocks, and sellers and closing agents often forget a few of them.

  • A Declaration of Value, required for deeds, contracts, assignments of contracts and quit claim deeds unless the document is exempt.
  • Transfer (revenue) tax on the full sale price over $500, or a stated exemption on the face of the document under Iowa Code chapter 428A.2.
  • A groundwater hazard statement, or a sentence saying the transaction is exempt. Since July 1, 2022, a seller may skip the statement if none of the listed conditions exist on the property.
  • A Prepared by block with name, address and telephone, plus an Address tax statement block with name, address and zip code, placed below the blank space required at the top of the page.
  • A complete legal description.

The owner answers for the accuracy of the groundwater statement. For questions, ask a realtor or an attorney. The Iowa Department of Natural Resources posts the form.

sections.h2: How a cash sale works with taxes due
sections.html:
A cash sale follows the same title steps as any other sale, minus the lender and the appraisal. Those are two common sources of delay.

Before closing, the closing agent checks the Treasurer's record for unpaid installments and any tax sale certificate. An open installment is paid from your proceeds. If a certificate has been issued, its holder must be paid and released before the deed can clear.

Some situations come up often in Scott County:

  • An inherited Davenport house with the last installment unpaid and nobody living in it.
  • A rental in a river-town neighborhood with deferred repairs that make a bank appraisal difficult.
  • A house split between two heirs in different states who cannot agree on repairs.

If one of these sounds like yours, send us the address and a short note about the tax status. We will tell you whether the parcel is in the county or the Davenport assessment system and what we need to see before we write an offer.

faqs.q: Who sends the property tax bill in Scott County?
faqs.a: The Scott County Treasurer collects property tax for the county, cities, schools and other taxing bodies. Assessments come from the Scott County Assessor, or from the Davenport City Assessor if the house is inside Davenport.

faqs.q: What are the Scott County property tax due dates?
faqs.a: The first installment is due September 30 and the second is due March 31 of the following year. A date on a weekend or holiday moves to the next business day.

faqs.q: Can I pay Scott County property tax online?
faqs.a: Yes. The Treasurer accepts e-checks and credit cards online, with a $0.25 e-check fee and a 2.25% credit card fee. Cash and debit cards are not accepted online.

faqs.q: When is the Scott County tax sale?
faqs.a: The annual tax sale is held on the third Monday of June, and delinquent taxes are published in June before that date.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Scott County house with unpaid property tax?
faqs.a: Yes. Unpaid taxes are paid from the sale proceeds at closing. Get a current payoff from the Treasurer before you accept any offer so you know how much will be deducted.
